core.title: Point hypermedia request constructs at same-origin paths, never absolute URLs
core.given: Scanned markup (a markup template, or source that can emit markup) contains a request-issuing markup construct — the stack's declarative construct that makes an element issue an HTTP request (from the profile).
core.when: The agent works in that code; every such request construct present is in scope, including existing unchanged ones.
core.then: Every request-issuing markup construct MUST address a same-origin path (root-relative, e.g. /api/orders, resolved against the document's origin) and MUST NOT carry an absolute (http://, https://) or protocol-relative (//host/…) URL.
prefer: Replace the absolute URL in the request construct's endpoint value with the same-origin path.
If the upstream is genuinely remote, expose a same-origin boundary route whose handler calls the upstream, so the origin decision lives in one auditable place.
Use the same-origin path form for every hypermedia control in the app.
avoid: Baking a foreign, staging or third-party host into a request-issuing markup construct.
Scattering cross-origin decisions across markup instead of one server-side boundary route.
Suppressing a foreign-origin endpoint finding — it is not suppressible.
unless: Path-only values (/orders, ./orders, orders) are same-origin and never flagged.
Markup attributes that do not issue requests (they carry selectors and modifiers, not endpoints) are out of scope.
core.why: A hypermedia client swaps the response markup straight into the live DOM with no parse step, so the endpoint origin is a trust boundary: a foreign origin fails three ways — the cross-origin call breaks once the other origin stops sending permissive headers, it is an untrusted-HTML injection point, and a baked-in staging host reaches production invisible to env vars and config review.
evidence: The check reports no request construct whose endpoint value begins http://, https:// or // anywhere in the scanned markup and source (existing and new).
Any genuinely required cross-origin call is reachable only via a same-origin boundary route whose handler performs the upstream call.
verification: Scope: the check scans the whole set of markup artifacts and source files that can carry request constructs — the profile's markup kinds and file suffixes — existing and new, not only the current diff; findings on unchanged existing constructs count and must be surfaced to activation.

Flag a request-issuing markup construct (the profile's request constructs) whose endpoint value begins http://, https:// or //; never flag path-only values, and ignore markup attributes that do not issue requests.
Out of check scope: server-side handler code calling a remote upstream from behind a same-origin boundary route.
Disposition strict, severity 2: a foreign-origin endpoint finding is not suppressible.

values: request-construct endpoint value begins http://, https:// or //

fires: Markup (or source that emits markup) contains a request construct whose endpoint is an absolute URL, whether newly added or already present and unchanged.
A request construct carries a protocol-relative endpoint value (//host/path).
A request construct points at a staging or third-party host.
doesNotFire: A request construct carries a path-only endpoint (/orders, ./orders, orders).
Only markup attributes that do not issue requests are involved (selectors, modifiers).
Server-side handler code calls a remote upstream from behind a same-origin boundary route.

neutralityNotes: The URL forms kept verbatim in the core (root-relative path, http://, https://, //) are stack-neutral web syntax, not stack machinery. The hypermedia mechanism in 'why' (response markup swapped into the live DOM with no parse step) is stated generically for any hypermedia client; the concrete framework is named only in the realization. The 'language' activation fact and the detector/finding ids have no neutral equivalent and stay bunOnly: the neutral core is bound to a stack by the profile's request constructs, markup kinds and suffixes. The check's artifact surface is expressed only through idiom.markup_kinds and the suffix keys; whole-set, not-only-diff scanning of unchanged constructs is a property of the check itself and lives in core verification (per round-1 feedback, roots.scan is reserved for repository roots, which this rule does not need). The proxy-route preference is expressed at role level (a same-origin boundary route whose handler calls the upstream); the concrete server-construct example is bunOnly. No rule content was dropped: both exceptions, all three failure modes and the strict disposition survive in the core.
